opening.text: Hi! We’re missionaries from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Do you have a few minutes to talk about our beliefs?
opening.caption: Introduction

help.prompt: Answer in your own words, or use this reply.
answers: Sure, I have a few minutes. I’m a Christian myself.

topics.title: The word Mormon
topics.background: Read the lesson question as written. Your partner gives the lesson answer.

question.text: Why is the use or non-use of the word Mormon a good thing to bring up with your Mormon friend?
question.caption: Lesson 1 · Question 1

help.hint: Try answering from the lesson first. Tap Suggested responses to see the lesson answer.
answers: Because the Mormon church ran the “I’m a Mormon” campaign, and then in 2018 President Nelson taught that to remove the Lord’s name from the Lord’s Church is “a major victory for Satan.”

topics.title: First Vision accounts
topics.background: Read the lesson question as written. Your partner gives the lesson answer.

question.text: How many different first vision accounts does the LDS church recognize and how do they defend the differing accounts?
question.caption: Lesson 1 · Question 2

help.hint: Try answering from the lesson first. Tap Suggested responses to see the lesson answer.
answers: There are nine different documented first vision accounts. Many Mormons will say that the differing accounts can be harmonized, similar to how the four gospels are harmonized.

topics.title: The expected response
topics.background: Read the lesson question as written. Your partner gives the lesson answer.

question.text: Suppose you were to share with your Mormon friend that there were multiple first vision accounts. What kind of response should you expect from a Mormon regarding the multiple first vision accounts?
question.caption: Lesson 1 · Question 3

help.hint: The most common response will be likened to the idea that there is a harmony to be found within the accounts.
answers:
I would expect them to say the accounts describe the same experience from different angles, with details varying according to the audience and purpose—much like the four Gospels.

As a Christian, I agree that different details don’t automatically mean a contradiction. But saying the accounts can be harmonized doesn’t demonstrate that they fit together. I would ask, ‘Could we compare a specific difference and see whether the explanations actually resolve it?’

For example, the 1832 account says Joseph had already concluded that no denomination followed the biblical gospel. The 1838 account says he hadn’t considered that all the churches were wrong. How do those statements fit together?

topics.title: Can the First Vision Accounts Be Reconciled?
topics.background: Read the lesson question as written. Your partner gives the lesson answer.

question.text: The different accounts of Joseph Smith’s First Vision tell a consistent story, just with different details, what would you say or ask next?
question.caption: Lesson 1 · Question 4

help.hint: Use a question to help move your point. For example, you could ask, “Have you ever considered that the accounts present Joseph at different ages?” “Is it possible there were multiple first visions?” If there were multiple “first visions,” only one was really the first, and that is not what the LDS church teaches. Guide them into discovering the problem for themselves.
answers:
Different details don’t automatically make accounts contradictory. But we need to examine whether particular statements fit together.

For example, in the 1832 account, Joseph says he had already concluded from Scripture that no denomination followed the gospel. In the 1838 account, he says it hadn’t occurred to him that all the churches were wrong.

How do you reconcile those statements? Was he going to pray already convinced that none was right, or was that something he learned through the vision? That matters when evaluating his claim that God called him to restore the Church.

topics.title: Someone unaware of the accounts
topics.background: Read the lesson question as written. Your partner gives the lesson answer.

question.text: How would you respond if your Mormon friend or neighbor was unaware that there were multiple first vision accounts?
question.caption: Lesson 1 · Question 5

help.hint: You would want to let them know, and provide references to, the various first vision accounts. You might even wish to begin with the church’s admission as such in the presentation at the Church History Museum in Salt Lake City, Utah, across from Temple Square and the Salt Lake Temple.
answers:
Your church publishes several accounts of the First Vision. For example, the 1832 account describes seeing the Lord and receiving forgiveness, but doesn’t explicitly describe the Father appearing alongside Jesus. The 1838 account explicitly describes two personages.

There’s another difference: in 1832, Joseph says he had already concluded from Scripture that no denomination followed the gospel. In 1838, he says he hadn’t considered that all the churches were wrong.

Could we read those accounts together? These differences raise questions for me about how reliable the story is. How do you understand them?

closing.text: Thanks for talking with me. I’ve enjoyed hearing what you think. Have a good evening!
closing.caption: Wrap up conversation

items.label: James 1:2–6
items.context: James encourages believers facing trials to ask God for wisdom, in faith. Joseph Smith said verse 5 led him to pray.

verses.text: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;
Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.
But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.
If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.

sourceNotes: Version 5: questions 3, 4 and 5 have new suggested responses that name the 1832 and 1838 differences and invite comparing the accounts; the course’s answer-key text for each moves to the hint (the harmony response for question 3; the rejoinder for question 4, shortened to fit the hint limit; the Church History Museum suggestion for question 5). Question 4 has a new title, “Can the First Vision Accounts Be Reconciled?”, and new wording. Version 4: the missionary role is named “LDS Missionary” in labels and instructions; spoken lines are unchanged. Lesson 1 v2: the course’s exact worksheet questions and answer key (lesson-one-exact-scenario.md, 21 October 2026), in worksheet order, between the existing introduction and goodbye. Questions are the Mormon’s lines; answers are the Christian’s single suggested response, hidden until asked for. No learning notes, evidence panels, scripture links or reading links in the help; the one passage is kept only because the content format requires at least one. Typos fixed: “bring up you’re your” to “bring up with your”, “do the LDS church” to “does”, “document” to “documented”, “firs vision” to “first vision”, plus small punctuation. Accuracy changes kept from v1: answer 1 drops the answer key’s unverified $6.1 million figure and the claim that the campaign ended the same year, and quotes President Nelson exactly (October 2018, The Correct Name of the Church: “To remove the Lord’s name from the Lord’s Church is a major victory for Satan.”) instead of saying every use of “Mormon” is a victory for Satan. Answer 4 keeps “multiple first visions” only as a question the Christian could ask, not as a historical claim; the different ages are 15 (a scribe’s addition to the 1832 account, “sixteenth year”) and about 14 in later accounts. Answer 5 keeps the course’s Church History Museum suggestion as written. The wrap-up beat uses the app’s fixed closing id “closing”.
